correctness.rationale: Homogeneity makes every convex order-and-equivalence extension diagram one complete type. An increasing anonymous new tuple has independent within-represented-class placements (1-z)^-(n+k) and, in each of k+1 quotient gaps, a sequence of nonempty unrepresented E-classes ((1-z)/(1-2z)). Their product proves the all-arity formula including n=k=0. Logarithmic derivatives verify t1,t2 and a genuine inversion. Ordered positive compositions give binomial fibre sizes; the central binomial estimate and small counterexamples establish sharpness. Same-class channel counts have the stated stars-and-bars formula; their first k values recover power sums and the size multiset via Newton identities. The extracted standalone checker directly enumerates 272 finite extension diagrams and 5,051 inversions; finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: This determines exactly which finite-base information the full all-arity numerical orbit spectrum does and does not retain in a classical homogeneous order. Two arities recover n,k optimally without knowing the base size; every other arity is redundant, yet the same spectrum has exponentially many different finite base order/isomorphism types. The simple definable anchored channel gives a finite-arity contrast recovering unordered class-size data. The sharp spectrum-fibre census and reconstruction contrast are structurally motivated, not an arbitrary slice or mere finite calculation.
